skill.name: webapp-testing
skill.description: Use Playwright to inspect, test, and debug local web applications in a real browser.

content.value_statement: Frontend changes need validation in a real browser, not only static checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Playwright-based testing, debugging, screenshots, and console inspection.
actual_capabilities: Guide browser navigation to local URLs with Playwright.
Support clicking, form filling, dropdown selection, dialogs, and alerts.
Verify page titles, visible elements, text content, URLs, and responsive behavior.
Capture local screenshots for debugging failed UI states.
Inspect browser console logs and network requests during testing.
limitations: Requires Node.js and a Playwright-capable environment.
Requires the target web application to be running or reachable.
Does not test native mobile applications.
Complex authentication flows may need project-specific setup.

use_cases.title: Verify a frontend change
use_cases.description: Run a browser workflow after changing UI behavior and confirm the expected page state appears.

use_cases.title: Debug a failed user journey
use_cases.description: Capture screenshots, console messages, and browser state to understand why a form or navigation flow fails.

use_cases.title: Check responsive behavior
use_cases.description: Exercise the same page across viewport sizes and confirm important controls remain visible and usable.

prompt_templates.title: Open the app and check the page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to open my local app, confirm the home page loads, and report the page title and any console errors.

prompt_templates.title: Test a form flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to fill the login form with test credentials, submit it, and verify whether the expected destination page appears.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a broken interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to reproduce the failing button click, capture a screenshot, inspect console logs, and explain the likely cause.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a responsive user journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the webapp-testing skill to test the checkout flow on desktop and mobile widths, verify key elements, and summarize any differences.

output_examples.input: Check whether the dashboard loads at my local app URL.
output_examples.output: The dashboard loaded successfully. The page title matched the expected app name, the main navigation was visible, and no console errors appeared.

output_examples.input: Find out why the submit button does not work.
output_examples.output: The button was visible but the click did not navigate. The browser console showed a validation error, and the screenshot showed an empty required field.

output_examples.input: Verify the page at mobile width.
output_examples.output: The mobile viewport rendered correctly overall. The primary action remained visible, but the footer overlapped the final form field.

best_practices: Start with a simple page load check before testing complex flows.
Use stable selectors such as roles or data-testid attributes.
Capture screenshots and console logs when a browser test fails.
anti_patterns: Do not test production accounts or real customer data without approval.
Do not rely only on brittle CSS class selectors when better selectors exist.
Do not skip waits after navigation or asynchronous UI updates.

faq.question: What does this skill help test?
faq.answer: It helps test local web application behavior through Playwright browser automation.

faq.question: Does it install Playwright?
faq.answer: The skill says Playwright can be installed automatically if it is not already present.

faq.question: Can it inspect browser console logs?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes guidance for collecting console messages during browser sessions.

faq.question: Can it test native mobile apps?
faq.answer: No. The skill is for web applications, not native mobile applications.

faq.question: Does it upload screenshots?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The skill describes saving local screenshots for debugging.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
